title: An AI agent embedded directly inside Minecraft as a live game environment
author: Leading-Leopard-7252
selftext:
I’ve been working on an experimental project that uses Minecraft as a real, running environment for an AI agent — not as a UI layer, but as the actual space the agent exists and operates in.

Instead of issuing one-off commands, the agent stays present in the world: observing game state, planning multi-step actions, executing them, and adapting when things fail.

Some of the things it can do:

* interact through natural voice input or chat
* plan and carry out multi-step tasks inside the game
* recover from failures instead of stopping
* function inside heavily modded worlds without hardcoded item logic

What I’m most interested in is how agent behavior changes when the environment is persistent, interactive, and imperfect — closer to a real game loop than a tool-based setup.

The project is open source and still evolving. I’d love feedback from people here experimenting with AI in games, simulations, or embodied environments.

Repo + demo:  
[https://github.com/aaronaalmendarez/gemini-minecraft](https://github.com/aaronaalmendarez/gemini-minecraft)

comments.author: Leading-Leopard-7252
comments.body:
Quick note: this is still very much an evolving project, and I’m mainly using it as a testbed for experimenting with agent orchestration in game environments.

If anyone here is working on similar ideas (agents in simulations, games, or persistent worlds), I’d genuinely love feedback — whether that’s architecture thoughts, edge cases, or “this would be cooler if it did X.”

Happy to answer questions about how it’s structured too.
